review.tagline: Policy-enforced sandbox runtime for autonomous agents with credential brokering
review.summary: Runs each agent in a sandbox with kernel-enforced limits on file access and system calls; every outbound connection passes a policy check, and agents never see real credentials, which a gateway injects only for approved endpoints. Policy changes are checked with formal verification before approval. Installs via a shell script on Linux, Apple Silicon macOS or WSL 2; Helm for Kubernetes; SDKs for Python, TypeScript, Go and Rust.
review.audience: Platform teams running fleets of autonomous agents
strengths: Credentials attached by the gateway only to approved endpoints; sandboxes never hold them
Formal verification flags risky new access before a policy change is applied
Kubernetes deployment via Helm; GPU use inside sandboxes documented
Python, TypeScript, Go and Rust SDKs plus agent skills via npx skills add
weaknesses: Windows support is WSL 2 only and experimental
Default sandbox image is minimal Ubuntu with no agent; running one follows the docs walkthrough
Anonymous telemetry on by default; disable with OPENSHELL_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false
Kubernetes installs require a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy
needs: Needs Docker, Podman or host virtualization
Models: any provider via routed inference credentials
